C10 and C04 share the limitations/finality/private-relief framework, but lack C07's distinctive customs machinery.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"the brokerage firm was apprised and ... could have protested within 60 days","parent_excerpt":"The importer failed to protest this ruling within sixty days after liquidation of the entry.","explanation":"Both make failure to invoke the same 60-day customs protest mechanism central to disapproval."},{"child_excerpt":"The claimants requested that certain oil field equipment be entered under provisions of the Tariff Act affording duty-free status","parent_excerpt":"similar merchandise was entitled to entry free of duty under paragraph 1622 of the Tariff Act","explanation":"Both frame the underlying dispute as a Tariff Act duty-free-entry claim involving a customs brokerage firm."},{"child_excerpt":"Statutes of limitations should be set aside only when justified by compelling equitable considerations. No such considerations appear here.","parent_excerpt":"This provision, like other statutes of limitations, is desirable to permit the final disposition of cases in an orderly manner.","explanation":"The child adapts C07's limitations-and-finality rationale into a concise equitable-considerations formulation."},{"child_excerpt":"the notice was properly sent to the brokerage firm as the party liable for the payment of duty","parent_excerpt":"the decision of the collector is final and conclusive upon the importer and all other persons","explanation":"Both analyze the legal responsibility of the customs-side claimant rather than treating administrative notice or later proof as grounds for exceptional relief."}]}
